Plotting against me? Ruining my life? No, I wouldn't say they're trying to ruin my life. I mean, I already told you about the hospital people and the cleaning agency folks watching me, tracking my routes. But plotting to ruin everything? No, I don't think so. It's just the watching. Which is stressful enough, let me tell you. It makes me so tired. Speaking of being tired, I had the hardest time sleeping last night. My husband was snoring so loudly. He usually doesn't snore unless he sleeps on his back, but no matter how many times I nudged him to roll over, he just kept rolling right back. I finally had to get up and go sleep in the guest room. The bed in there is a little too firm for my liking, though. We bought that mattress at a discount furniture place out on the highway. The salesman was wearing the most garish plaid suit I've ever seen. It was green and yellow, like a bruised banana. I don't know who told him that looked good. He tried to sell us a matching bedroom set with all this ornate carving on it, but I told him, "Who's going to dust all those little grooves?" That's the thing people don't think about when they buy fancy furniture. You have to keep it clean. And dust settles everywhere. It's like it has a mind of its own. But anyway, no, nobody is plotting to ruin my life, just the watching.

Hidden messages on the TV? No, I don't think so. I mostly just watch the morning news and the weather anyway. The weather is so important when you're cleaning houses, you know? Well, yes, absolutely. I'm here because people keep acting like I'm imagining it, but I know it's true. I know the hospital people and some folks from the agency have been watching our house and following my cleaning routes to see if I'm taking proper care of my husband. We had a terrible winter last year, didn't we? The snow just kept coming down. I had to shovel the driveway three times in one day just so the mail carrier could get to the box. He's a nice young man, the mail carrier, always leaves a little dog treat for the neighbor's poodle, even though that dog yaps at him every time. But anyway, yes, they're watching me to see if I mess up with my husband, and it's just not right.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever believed that certain events, actions, or objects had a special or hidden meaning that was specifically directed at you, even if others didn't see it that way?\n\nPatient: Special or hidden meanings? No, I don't think so. A broom is just a broom, you know? Although, speaking of brooms, I had to buy a new one last week because the bristles on my old one were getting all bent and frayed. They always have exactly what you need, and the owner, Mr. Higgins, he knows where everything is. You just tell him you need a half-inch galvanized screw, and he walks right over to the exact drawer. It’s amazing. He’s been running that place for, oh, it must be forty years now. His grandson works there on the weekends. Nice boy, tall, plays basketball for the high school. They made it to the state semi-finals last year, which was a really big deal for the town. Everyone put up signs in their yards to support the team. I didn't put one up, though, because I don't want to draw any extra attention to the house, what with the people watching and all. But no, I haven't noticed any special meanings in things. Just normal things.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever believed that others were secretly plotting against you or trying to ruin your life, even if they weren’t physically threatening you or trying to harm you directly?\n\nPatient: Plotting against me? But plotting to ruin everything? No, I don't think so. It's just the watching. Which is stressful enough, let me tell you. It makes me so tired. Speaking of being tired, I had the hardest time sleeping last night. My husband was snoring so loudly. He usually doesn't snore unless he sleeps on his back, but no matter how many times I nudged him to roll over, he just kept rolling right back. I finally had to get up and go sleep in the guest room. The bed in there is a little too firm for my liking, though. We bought that mattress at a discount furniture place out on the highway. The salesman was wearing the most garish plaid suit I've ever seen. It was green and yellow, like a bruised banana. I don't know who told him that looked good. But he retired and moved to Florida a few years ago. I think everyone moves to Florida eventually, don't they? The humidity down there would ruin my hair, though. But anyway, no, I don't know why they're watching me. I haven't done anything to deserve it.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt that things that other people do or say—like conversations, actions, or events happening around you—were somehow secretly about you or meant something special for you, even if they didn’t seem connected to you at first glance?\n\nPatient: No, I can't say I've ever noticed anything like that. People mostly just mind their own business, unless they're the ones watching me, of course. But strangers talking or things happening on the news? No, that's just normal life. Speaking of the news, did you see that segment they did on the local channel about the new recycling rules? It is just getting so complicated. You can't put glass in the blue bins anymore, you have to take it to a separate drop-off center. And don't even get me started on the plastics. It has to be a number one or a number two, and you have to wash them out completely. I spend half my evening just scrubbing out peanut butter jars. Peanut butter is the absolute worst to get out. My husband loves that chunky kind, the natural one where the oil separates at the top? You have to stir it for five minutes just to make a sandwich. I tried buying him the regular creamy kind once, just to save myself the hassle of stirring it, but he wouldn't touch it. Said it tasted too sweet. He's very particular about his food. He likes his toast just barely browned, almost warm bread, really. If it gets even a little bit dark, he'll scrape it with a butter knife over the sink. The crumbs go everywhere. I have to wipe down the counter three times a day just to keep up with the crumbs. I use those Clorox wipes, the lemon-scented ones. They cut through the grease really well, especially around the stove. But no, I don't think regular people are talking about me secretly or anything like that.\n\nDoctor: Have there been times when you felt down, hopeless, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy, even for just a few days at a time?\n\nPatient: No, I don't think so. I don't really have the time to sit around feeling down or hopeless, to be honest. I'm always on the go, keeping busy with my houses. Tomorrow I have to go over to Mrs. Gable's place, and let me tell you, that is a full day's work right there. She has these heavy velvet curtains in her living room, floor to ceiling. Velvet is just terrible for holding onto dust. You can't just shake them out, you have to use the upholstery attachment on the vacuum and go over every single inch. \n\nMy old Hoover finally gave out on me last month doing exactly that. The belt just snapped right in the middle of a job. It made this horrible burning rubber smell, filled the whole room. It smelled exactly like when my husband tried to fix the alternator on his old Chevy truck and left a rag too close to the engine block. That truck is his baby. It's an '85, sky blue, though the paint is peeling right off the hood now. He says it gives it character, but I think it just looks messy. I keep telling him to park it in the garage to protect it from the weather, but there's no room. The garage is completely filled with his woodworking tools. He started making these little cedar birdhouses last spring. They really are cute, he paints the little roofs red and everything, but the sawdust gets absolutely everywhere. It tracks right into the kitchen on his boots. I have to sweep the linoleum twice a day sometimes, and don't even get me started on when it gets into the grout. But no, I don't get down or lose interest in things. There's just too much to do.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever believed that certain everyday events, like something you saw, heard, or read, were secretly meant for you or had a special message for you, even if others didn't see it that way?\n\nPatient: No, I don't think so. I mean, when I read the paper or look at the mail, it's just regular stuff. Mostly it's just junk mail these days anyway, isn't it? So many catalogs and coupons. I do clip the coupons, though, especially the ones for cleaning supplies. You wouldn't believe how expensive Windex has gotten. I tried using the generic store brand once, the one from Kroger? It left terrible streaks on the glass. I was cleaning the big bay window at the Henderson's house—they have this gorgeous house over in the Heights, right on the corner. It gets so much afternoon sun, which is lovely, but it shows every single streak on that glass. If you don't use the name brand and a proper microfiber cloth, it just looks a mess when the sun hits it at four o'clock. And they have these heavy oak blinds... dusting those is an absolute nightmare. You have to tilt them one way, wipe every single slat, and then tilt them the other way. My wrist aches just thinking about it. I have a little bit of arthritis starting in my right wrist, right at the joint. The doctor told me to wear a brace at night, but it's so clunky I can't sleep with it on. It catches on the sheets. I buy those high-thread-count sheets whenever they go on sale at the department store, they're just so much softer against the skin... but anyway, no, no secret messages or anything like that. Just regular everyday things.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever believed that you were chosen for a special purpose or had a unique role that no one else could fulfill, something that others might not understand or believe?\n\nPatient: Well, yes, actually. I mean, not like a superhero or anything silly like that, but... a while back, I just started feeling like I was the only one with the sense and the strength to keep my husband, my home, and even some of the folks at church safe from what was coming. It just felt like everything rested on my shoulders, you know? Like I was the only one who could see how important it was to be prepared. \n\nSpeaking of being prepared, I was just telling Mrs. Gable yesterday that she needs to stock up on canned goods. You never know with the weather these days. We had that terrible ice storm back in '98, do you remember? We were out of power for four days. I had to cook all the meat in the freezer on the camp stove out on the back porch so it wouldn't spoil. My husband was so mad because I used up all the propane he bought for his hunting trip. He goes up to the cabin every November with his brothers. They never actually shoot anything, they just sit around playing poker and drinking cheap beer. He brought back a cooler full of venison sausage once, but it was so gamey I couldn't even put it in spaghetti sauce. I usually make my own sauce from scratch, with San Marzano tomatoes. You have to crush them by hand to get the right texture. The canned crushed ones are just too watery. If you don't simmer it for at least four hours, it just doesn't taste right. I like to add a little pinch of sugar to cut the acidity, my grandmother taught me that. She used to have this huge garden out back... but yes, I just knew I was the only one who could keep everyone safe. It's a heavy burden, really."
